subject: Atlas Commerce — POC kickoff & workload confirmation (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Sally Huang <sally@atlascommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Atlas Commerce — POC kickoff & workload confirmation (post-call recap)

Hi Sally — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the kickoff: 

Call takeaways:
- Primary goal: validate inference economics & latency for Atlas Search autocomplete + summary pipeline (customer-facing).
- Key integrations: live REST API (no heavy streaming), occasional batched re-rank jobs.

What we need from you (confirm by EOD Wed):
- Workload snapshot: avg prompt/completion token counts, typical QPS/RPS, peak bursts (duration/shape).
- Acceptance criteria: performance targets and any non-functional requirements (data retention, redaction, SOC2 constraints).

Redwood proposed POC plan (high-level):
1) Intake & baseline (this week): exchange workload sample + Redwood POC intake template (attached).
2) Kickoff + environment setup (week of Jan 25): test harness, traffic replay, and test dataset ingestion.
3) Trial run (2 weeks): synthetic replay + small pilot on live traffic if you approve.
4) Readout & signoff: run success criteria and discuss next steps (Dedicated/private options if needed).

Suggested success criteria (initial):
- 95th percentile tail latency for inference < 300 ms (end-to-end token generation).
- Sustained throughput: support sustained 60 RPS with concurrency target 30; tolerate bursts to 900 RPS for up to 10 minutes with graceful degradation/fallback.
- Cost target: baseline unit cost < $0.005 per 1k tokens (placeholder — we'll firm this up once we see exact token mix).
- Functional correctness: acceptable extraction/summary quality on your dev prompt set (we'll add a small eval pass).

Attachments: redwood_poc-template.docx (POC intake + measurement template). Please fill the short table on page 2 with the sample traffic profile.

Proposed kickoff slot: Jan 25, 09:00 PT — will hold tentative invite if that works for you.

Thanks — tagging Marissa and Dev to help with the technical intake and test harness.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com

From: Sally Huang <sally@atlascommerce.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 10:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Atlas Commerce — POC kickoff & workload confirmation (post-call recap)

Thanks Priya — appreciate the clear plan. Attaching a small sample of our traffic and answers to your intake fields below. I've also looped in Tom Becker (platform lead) for technical constraints.

Workload summary (sample):
- Avg prompt tokens: 50
- Avg completion tokens: 120
- Typical sequence length (prompt+completion): ~170 tokens
- Sustained RPS: 60
- Peak (observed): bursts to ~900 RPS lasting up to 8–12 minutes (marketing surges)
- Typical concurrency: ~25–35 active sessions during peak windows
- Percent streaming: ~5% (mostly synchronous requests)
- Re-rank batch jobs: 5–10 jobs per hour, each ~5000 items; not latency-critical but important for throughput.

Data/security notes:
- PII: we can provide a redacted sample; any live testing must respect our retention policy (14 days) and avoid storing raw customer emails.
- SOC2: Atlas is SOC2-compliant; will need evidence of Redwood controls during intake (scope doc ok).

Attachments: atlas_workload_sample.csv (small anonymized sample).

Kickoff: Jan 25 at 09:00 PT works for our team — please send the invite.

-- Sally
Sally Huang
Product Manager, Atlas Commerce
sally@atlascommerce.com

Thanks for the details, Sally — helpful. A few clarifying Qs + proposed owners/measurements so we can turn this into an actionable intake: 

Clarifying questions:
- Can you confirm the percent of requests that include attachments or large context (>1k tokens)?
- For the re-rank batch jobs, do you require near-real-time ranking (within 1–2s) or is 10–30s acceptable?

Proposed measurable success criteria (to refine at kickoff):
1) Performance: 95th pctl latency < 300ms for single-shot generation at production token mix.
2) Scalability: sustain 60 RPS for 2+ hours without degradation; handle burst to 900 RPS for 10 minutes with predefined fallback to cheaper model if needed.
3) Cost: < $0.006 per 1k tokens at trial utilization (we'll produce a per-token breakdown during baseline).
4) Functionality: automated eval on your gold prompts — target F1/completeness threshold > 0.9 for named-entity extraction tasks used by Search.

Owners:
- Redwood test harness & baseline: Dev Patel (dev_patel@redwood.com)
- Trial orchestration & reporting: Marissa Cole (marissa_cole@redwood.com)
- Atlas signoff: Sally (PM) + Tom (Platform)

Operational asks before kickoff:
- Provide the anonymized traffic CSV (thanks for attaching).
- Identify a small set of evaluation prompts (5–10) for functional checks.
- Confirm whether you'd like us to attempt a brief live pilot on day 3 of the trial (we can do a scoped canary).

I'll prep the trial-run checklist and traffic replay steps and share it to the Drive link in the final note.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole

Quick note from platform/security: we need the following on the table before any live traffic testing:
- A short scoped data handling doc that describes what Redwood will log/retain during the trial (we can accept redacted logs).
- Confirmation that any PII is removed from the test payloads.
- SOC2 evidence (summary is fine) or a standard security questionnaire — we can share our vendor intake form if helpful.

If those are in place, we are fine to proceed with a canary on day 3. We're keen to watch the model behavior on the 900-RPS bursts; please make sure your fallback/queueing behavior is documented.

Thanks — Tom
